extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, journalists, scientists, journal editors, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: News/blog coverage and documentation of allegations, investigations, institutional responses, and journal actions in cases of scientific and medical research misconduct. Focuses on factual timeline, examples of alleged breaches, and consequences (expressions of concern, retractions, disciplinary or legal action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical permission for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: “had never obtained ethical permission to conduct his experiments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page reports that lack of ethical approval for experimental procedures is a central allegation; publicity about absent approvals can force institutional inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate reporting of study outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: “had misrepresented the outcome of Beyene’s implant.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misrepresenting clinical outcomes in publications is treated as serious misconduct and is cited as grounds for expressions of concern and retraction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent must be obtained prior to procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: “only Beyene had signed a consent form—and the form was dated two weeks after his surgery.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent forms signed after an intervention (or absent consent) are presented as a major ethical violation; such timing undermines validity of consent and supports misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of whistleblowers / prohibition of retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Retaliation against the whistleblowers came quickly. … told that they had violated patient privacy and would be fired immediately. … the Karolinska Institute informed the whistleblowers that the head of the cardiothoracic clinic would deliver a formal warning.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative treats institutional retaliation (threats of firing, formal warnings, police involvement) as an anti-pattern; whistleblowers should not be punished for raising concerns and institutions should avoid actions that amount to intimidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional responsibility to investigate and act on misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: “Anders Hamsten, the vice‑chancellor, said he would ask for an external inquiry.”  “KI is also calling to retract six articles co‑authored by Macchiarini and his colleagues.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are expected to initiate or commission external inquiries and, when misconduct is substantiated, to request retractions and take corrective steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals should issue expressions of concern and retract when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: References to journals issuing “expressions of concern” and later retracting papers (e.g., The Lancet retracts two papers; Respiration later retracted a 2015 paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline shows journals may first flag concerns and then retract papers after investigations or institutional requests; delayed action is documented as part of the saga.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct includes serious inaccuracies and misleading information in articles
rubrics_metrics.description: “KI’s investigation uncovered ‘serious inaccuracies and misleading information in the reviewed articles.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of serious inaccuracies/misleading statements in publications are characterized as concrete bases for misconduct determinations and retraction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal noted the data presented in a paper may not be “fully representative” of the experiments; Macchiarini blamed KI for losing data as he retracts a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about data completeness, representativeness, or availability are cited as reasons for expressions of concern and retraction; loss or questionable handling of data undermines trust in published results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship accountability and removal by co‑authors
rubrics_metrics.description: “Over time, multiple authors have asked to be removed from the paper.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co‑authors requesting removal from a paper is presented as an indicator of problems with the integrity of the work and may accompany institutional actions to retract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal accountability for patient harm
rubrics_metrics.description: “sentenced to 30 months in prison for causing bodily harm to his patients.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents that egregious research/clinical misconduct that causes patient harm can lead not only to professional sanctions and retractions but also to criminal prosecution and imprisonment.
